script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

INT. UNIVERSITY CAFETERIA - DAY

A sea of students fill the noisy cafeteria. JORDAN, 25, sits alone, his eyes glued to a sports highlight reel on his phone.

WAITRESS
(approaching)
What can I get for you today, Jordan?

JORDAN
(upset)
Just a coffee.

She sets the coffee down and watches him.

WAITRESS
You look down. Everything okay?

JORDAN
(sighs)
Just a bad day. I thought I'd be further in my career by now.

WAITRESS
(smiling)
You have time. I know a man who used to be in your shoes. He's doing great now. He's a tennis coach at our community center.

EXT. COMMUNITY TENNIS COURT - LATER

Jordan arrives, hesitant. COACH SAM, 50, greets him warmly. They play a friendly game of tennis.

COACH SAM
(after game)
You have a natural talent, Jordan.

JORDAN
(smiling)
I thought my time had passed.

COACH SAM
(laughs)
It's never too late to start. I wish I had started earlier. Come work with me.

INT. COMMUNITY TENNIS CENTER - DAY

Jordan starts volunteering as a coach. He struggles at first but begins to connect with students.

INT. JORDAN'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jordan's roommate JASON teases him about his new career.

JASON
You, coaching tennis? Are you serious?

JORDAN
(defensive)
It's not a joke. I'm good at it.

JASON
(laughs)
Suit yourself.

INT. TENNIS TOURNAMENT - DAY

Jordan and Coach Sam take their students to a tournament. Jordan coaches a shy girl, EMMA, who has never won a match.

EMMA
(anxiously)
I can't do this.

JORDAN
(encouraging)
You can, Emma. Believe in yourself.

EMMA wins her first match, surprising everyone. Jordan feels a sense of accomplishment.

EXT. TENNIS COURT - NIGHT

Jordan sits on the grass, watching his students play. He looks up as Coach Sam approaches.

COACH SAM
(smiling)
You've found your place, Jordan.

JORDAN
(smiling back)
I have.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - DAY

Jordan stands in front of a class, leading a lesson. He looks confident and in his element.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
